resources.string: Helium is less dense than air and is used to inflate balloons.
Gold-coated beryllium mirrors are used in the Webb telescope. The gold is a coating.
Nitrogen is essential to plant growth. Fertilisers provide nitrogen-containing compounds.
Oxygen supports cellular respiration. The lungs illustrate its exchange with air.
Fluoride compounds help protect tooth enamel; this is not an application of fluorine gas.
Magnesium burns with a brilliant light and is used in pyrotechnics.
Aluminium can be rolled into thin sheets used for packaging.
Chlorine and chlorine-containing disinfectants are used in water treatment. The droplet represents water.
Argon protects the filament in incandescent bulbs. The hot filament produces the light.
Scandium is added to aluminium alloys used in lightweight bicycle frames.
Vanadium is used in alloy steels, including spring steels. This is not a pure vanadium spring.
Manganese dioxide is used in many batteries, including alkaline cells. The drawing illustrates this use.
Cobalt compounds colour glass and ceramic glazes blue. The vase is not cobalt metal.
Bananas contain potassium ions, as do many other foods; not potassium metal.
Skull: documented toxicity; depends on form and exposure. Badges are not an exhaustive hazard inventory.
Radioactive: no stable isotope. The badge does not indicate activity or danger level.
Material colours and textures guide this stylised composition; it is not a crystallographic model.
Red phosphorus: an amorphous form, shown as grains rather than crystal pillars.
Stibnite (Sb₂S₃) is an antimony ore. These needles illustrate the mineral, not pure antimony.
Heated iodine: dark crystalline solid and purple sublimation vapour.
Stepped crystals; a thin oxide layer produces the iridescent colours.
Six frames, living scenes · Drag the card to move the light
Deuterium (²H): one proton, one neutron, one electron. Common hydrogen-1 has no neutron. Schematic orbit.
Neutral helium-4: two protons, two neutrons and two electrons. Schematic orbit.
Lithium is used in rechargeable batteries. This drawing illustrates a use.
Table salt is sodium chloride (NaCl), a compound containing sodium; not sodium metal.
Bone mineral contains calcium phosphate, mainly hydroxyapatite.
Titanium alloys are used in aircraft structures and engines. The aircraft illustrates this use.
Chromium plating gives metal objects a polished, reflective finish.
Zinc coatings protect steel from corrosion. The shield symbolises galvanising.
Neodymium and samarium are used in permanent magnetic alloys. Symbolic shape.
The tree evokes carbon’s essential place in organic matter.
Pairs of identical atoms: N₂, O₂ or F₂. Colours and motion are schematic.
Nuclear research motif. No claim of an everyday use or visible bulk sample.
Mechanical alloy motif; the object is not made of the pure element.
Stylised research specimen; its shape and colours are illustrative.
Artistic motif: colours, glow and movement are stylised.

Potassium salts colour the flame lilac in a flame test.
Gallium melts at about 29.8 °C. This sample softens into a metallic pool.
Coins evoke historical silver currency, often alloyed with copper.
Tinplate is steel sheet coated with a thin layer of tin.
The setting evokes platinum jewellery alloys. The stone represents a diamond, not platinum.
Bullion bars illustrate the characteristic metallic colour of gold.
